Your final report should be no longer than **20 pages** in length with double-spaced text and including
any tables, figures, graphs, etc., but not including references, appendices, or a cover page.

There is no specific style to the report, however it should be well organized with appropriate
sections. 

# Introduction

Introduction includes a summary/ description of the project topic, relevant literature review, purpose and motivation of the work.


# Methods 

Methods section describes the methods used in the project. You do not need to explain the methods in detail, but should provide the essential aspects on each method along with their assumptions, why and how they are used. If you are including examples, you can introduce them here or in a separate section. 

# Results 

You can present your examples and simulation study in this section 

You can run your analysis in this rmd file but using `echo=FALSE`. This will mask all the code from your report but still evaluate them.  

Present your results using appropriate outputs such as tables and figures. Below are examples on how to code these and mask the \R codes. Note that any \R code written here will be placed automatically in Appendix at the end. 

Figure \ref{fig2} is generated using an R chunk.

```{r fig2, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5, fig.align='center', out.width="50%", fig.cap = "\\label{fig2}A meaningless scatterplot.", echo = FALSE}
plot(runif(25), runif(25))
```


Tables can also be generated using R chunks, as shown in Table \ref{tab1} for example.

```{r tab1, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(mtcars)[,1:4], 
    caption = "\\label{tab1}Caption centered above table."
)
```
